message.reasoning:
I am reviewing the current Monopoly game state to prepare a decision.

I have the orange monopoly and $658 cash. I will build houses evenly on St. James Place, Tennessee Avenue, and New York Avenue.

Two houses on each orange property will cost $600 and leave $58. Rent with two houses is $200 on St. James Place, $200 on Tennessee Avenue, and $220 on New York Avenue.

I need to build now. Player three has a pink monopoly and roughly $740, so they will likely place seven houses on St. Charles, States, and Virginia before my turn ends.

Pink two-house rent is $150 on St. Charles, $150 on States, and $180 on Virginia. Orange two-house rent is already higher at $200, $200, and $220. The orange three-house rent would jump to $550, $550, and $600, well above the pink $450, $450, and $500. I am weighing whether to trade for the extra $42 needed to build a seventh house.

I rejected selling Kentucky Avenue to player two because that would complete their red monopoly and let them build heavily. Short Line is not worth trading either. I am now considering whether to propose a trade for about fifty dollars.

I decided against trading for cash or unmortgaging properties. Unmortgaging would cost too much, and no opponent is likely to give me money for nothing. I will build two houses on each orange property now.

Player four now controls the yellow monopoly and utilities. Their cash is $560, but they likely spent about $143 to unmortgage Ventnor. That leaves roughly $417 for building yellow houses.

Player two still lacks a complete red monopoly and has no GOOJF. Player three controls the pink monopoly plus light blue properties.
